{{Short description|Inland Bikol language subgroup spoken in the Philippines}} {{Infobox language |name=Albay Bikol |states=[[Philippines]] |region=[[Bicol Region|Bicol]] |speakers=700,000; 300,000 of rbl; 260,000 of fbl; 73,600 of ubl; 68,800 of lbl |date=2009 SIL |ref={{e16|bhk}} |familycolor=Austronesian |fam2=[[Malayo-Polynesian languages|Malayo-Polynesian]] |fam3=[[Philippine languages|Philippine]] |fam4=[[Central Philippine languages|Central Philippine]] |fam5=[[Bikol languages]] |fam6=[[Inland Bikol]] |lc1=ubl|ld1=Boînën (Buhiʼnon) |lc2=lbl|ld2=Libon Bikol |lc3=rbl|ld3=Miraya Bikol |lc4=fbl|ld4=West Albay Bikol |glotto=alba1269 |glottorefname=Inland-Buhi-Daraga Bikol }} '''Albay Bikol''', or simply '''Albayanon''' is a group of languages and one of the three languages that compose [[Inland Bikol]]. It is spoken in the southwestern coast of [[Albay]], ([[Pio Duran]], [[Jovellar]]) and northwestern [[Sorsogon]]. The region is bordered by the [[Bikol language|Coastal Bikol]] and [[Rinconada Bikol]] speakers. The latter is the closest language of Albay Bikol and is mutually intelligible. They are both included in [[Inland Bikol]] group of languages.{{Cite book |last=Borja |first=Nhia |url=https://academicworks.cuny.edu/gc_etds/5781/ |title=Diaspora Documentation of West Albay Bikol |date=June 2024 |publisher=[[CUNY Graduate Center]] |language=en}}{{Citation |title=2 Bikol |date=2014-08-19 |work=Types of Reduplication: A Case Study of Bikol |pages=5–28 |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783110363128.5/html |access-date=2026-03-20 |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |language=en |doi=10.1515/9783110363128.5 |isbn=978-3-11-036312-8}}{{Cite web |title=About Albay {{!}} Province of Albay |url=https://albay.gov.ph/about/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250801054632/https://albay.gov.ph/about/ |archive-date=2025-08-01 |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=albay.gov.ph |language=en-US}}{{Cite journal |last=Magdato |first=Norma |date=October 2025 |title=Sustaining West Bikol: A Community-Based Language Perspective on Language Development |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396622187_Sustaining_West_Bikol_A_Community-Based_Language_Perspective_on_Language_Development |journal=R&D Journal |volume=28 |issue=1 |via=ResearchGate}} Albay Bikol is the only sub-group of the Inland Bikol group with several languages with in it. The member languages in this sub-grouping lack stressed syllables, rare, if there is, and that makes them different and unique from other Bikol languages. [[Central Bikol language|Coastal Bikol]] ! Boînën ([[Lake Buhi]]) ! Libon ! Oasnon/West Miraya ! Daraga/East Miraya ! [[Rinconada Bikol]] |- |{{Lang|bcl|Nahaloy ka duman sa saod?}} |{{Lang|ubl|Naëg̓ëy ika adto sa saran?}} |{{Lang|lbl|Naoban ika adtu sa sawod?}} |{{Lang|rbl|Naëlëy ka idto sa sëd?}} |{{Lang|rbl|Naëlay ka didto sa sâran?}} |{{Lang|bto|Naëban ika sadto saran?}} |- |} ==Orthography== Boînën has the following orthography for native vocabulary:Translators Association of the Philippines (2023) Ortograpiyang Boînën Aa Bb Dd Ëë Gg G̓g̓ Ii Kk Ll Mm Nn NGng Oo Pp Rr Ss Tt Ww Yy. ''Ë'' is used for {{IPA|/ə/}}, ''G̓'' for {{IPA|/ɰ/}}, and O for {{IPA|/ʊ/}}. Cc, Ee, Ff, Hh, Jj, Ññ, Qq, Uu, Vv, Xx, Zz only occur in loans and proper names. A circumflex accent is used for glottal stop at the end of a word or before a consonant, as in the name ''Boînën'' {{IPA|/bʊiʔnən/}}. Glottal stop is not written at the beginning of a word or between vowels; instead, a tie bar is used to mark the absence of a glottal stop in sequences where it might occur. This includes identical vowels, {{angbr|a͡a ë͡ë i͡i o͡o}}, and sequences that begin with /a/: {{angbr|a͡ë a͡i a͡o}}. For a front or back vowel followed by a central vowel, a Y or W is used: {{angbr|iya, iyë, owa, owë}}. This [[vowel hiatus]] frequently corresponds to a Tagalog {{angbr|h}} (e.g. Boînën ''ka͡oy'', Tagalog ''kahoy'' 'wood'). Both diacritics can occur, as in ''ba͡â'' 'flood'. Glottal stop can occur in the sequences that would otherwise take a tie bar (other than {{angbr|ii}}, as {{IPA|/iʔi/}} does not occur), and in addition occurs in {{angbr|ia ië}}. {| class=wikitable !Hiatus !!Glottal stop |- | a͡a || aa |- |ë͡ë |ëë |- |i͡i | |- |o͡o |oo |- |a͡ë |aë |- |a͡i |ai |- |a͡o |ao |- |iya |ia |- |iyë |ie |- |owa | |- |owë | |- |oi | |} ==See also== *[[Languages of the Philippines]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://bikoltranslator.blogspot.com Translate Bikol] *[https://manifold.uhpress.hawaii.edu/projects/bikol-text Bikol Text], [https://manifold.uhpress.hawaii.edu/projects/bikol-grammar-notes Bikol Grammar Notes], and [https://manifold.uhpress.hawaii.edu/projects/bikol-dictionary Bikol Dictionary] at the [[University of Hawaiʻi|University of Hawai‘i]] {{Wikivoyage|Buhi Bikol phrasebook|Buhi Bikol|a phrasebook}} {{incubator|rbl|lang=Miraya Bikol|3=ubl|lang2=Buhi'non Bikol}} {{Bikol languages}} {{Languages of the Philippines}} {{Philippine languages}} [[Category:Bikol languages]] [[Category:Languages of Albay]] [[Category:Languages of Camarines Sur]] [[Category:Languages of Sorsogon]]
